sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Sudhir Kumar Kulshrestha Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ashwani Kumar Mishra,J.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 87 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Chandapa, District Hathras.
Accused applicant is the husband of the deceased, who has died on account of burn injuries.
The first information report contains allegation with regard to demand of dowry and the complaint is that deceased has been done to death by the family members including the applicant.
Counsel for the applicant points out that the place of occurrence where deceased has been burnt to death is in front of rice mill belonging to one Mukesh Chauhan.
It is submitted that the deceased has not died within the house but has died at a distance of almost 250-300 meters from the house of the accused.
It is stated that accused applicant had taken the injured to the hospital and the police personnel also arrived on the statement of the accused applicant.
It is submitted that accused applicant is in jail since 9.6.2022 and has no criminal history.

It is also submitted that there are 16 Anil Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37106556/
1 witnesses in the chargesheet but only four of them have been examined.

sentences.text: Argument is that trial is likely to take sufficiently long to conclude and that the applicant undertakes that he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the conduct of trial.
Learned AGA states that the death has occurred within seven years of marriage and the accused applicant is the husband.

Be that as it may, considering the fact that accused applicant has no criminal history and is in Jail for the last more than two years and the conduct of trial may take sufficiently long as also the fact that the information of death was given by the applicant and he had also taken the injured to the hospital, without further commenting upon the merits of the case, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail, at this stage.
Above observations made in the bail order shall, however, not be construed as expression of opinion, on the merits, at the stage of trial.

Let the applicant - Anil Kumar involved in aforesaid case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned,
with the following conditions, which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
ii) The applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 269 of BNS.

(v) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 84 of BNSS. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 209 of BNS.

(vi) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 351 of BNSS.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance Anil Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37106556/
2 with law.

Accordingly, the present bail application is allowed.
